name: link-state-telnet

graded_by.test: owed by the E3 worker plan

description: The telnet liveness probe is IAC DO TIMING-MARK (RFC 860), sent when now − max(last E3, last probe) ≥ keepalive_probe_interval. A WILL, a WONT, an answer to any earlier probe, a second answer to one probe, and payload each count as E3. Each probe is sent whether or not an earlier one was answered: two probes in a row to a silent peer are both sent. A silent peer reaches missing, then link_timeout (now − last(E3) ≥ keepalive_interval × keepalive_count_max). With keepaliveInterval 0 no probe is sent and nothing fires; a target file sets it per target. When the target's socket closes with the session, the worker stops that connection's link timers and sends no further link_state for it. While the worker has stopped reading at buffer_bytes before open_shell, link_timeout is disarmed for that connection until open_shell: a reply the worker is deliberately not reading never counts as a dead link. U3 test, owed.

messages.note: the first event to a new control peer of a connected connection is link_state, so the core has the countdown at once
